# **Architectural and Data Dictionary Analysis of ARCA Forms 1116-C and 1116-B via the WSLPG Web Service**

## **The Electronic Grain Liquidation Framework under the ARCA Administration**

The agricultural commercialization framework in the Argentine Republic represents one of the most rigorously monitored commodity tracking systems in the global agrarian economy. This system is overseen by the domestic revenue service, recently reorganized and rebranded as the Agencia de Recaudación y Control Aduanero (ARCA), assuming the historical duties of the former AFIP administration.1 Within this highly regulated macroeconomic environment, the documentation of grain sales, purchases, and secondary transfers is managed through a specialized systemic infrastructure known officially as the Web Service Liquidación Primaria de Granos (WSLPG). The overarching objective of this system is to enforce real-time tax compliance, ensuring that every ton of agricultural produce is traced from its agronomic origin at the farm gate through to domestic processing facilities or export terminals.

The WSLPG architecture standardizes the electronic emission of operational documents, specifically mandating the use of Form 1116-C for Primary Grain Liquidations and Form 1116-B for Secondary Grain Liquidations. The regulatory stipulations outlining the structure, timing, and submission parameters of these electronic forms derive from General Resolutions RG 3419/12, which governs the issuance of Primary Liquidations, and RG 3690/14, which establishes the rules for Secondary Liquidations.2 Operating under a framework that is actively being updated for the 2025 and 2026 fiscal cycles, the architecture relies heavily on SOAP-based web services.4 Taxpayers, agricultural cooperatives, and grain elevators must interface with the endpoint defined by the Web Services Description Language (WSDL) at http://serviciosjava.afip.gob.ar/wslpg/LpgService?wsdl to declare their operations.5

This exhaustive research report presents a comprehensive, field-by-field structural analysis of Forms 1116-C and 1116-B as demanded by the current ARCA schema. The analysis details the stringent data typing constraints, maximum lengths, mandatory conditions, and the intricate business logic that dictates the mathematical cascading effects generating these critical tax documents.

## **Cryptographic Security Protocol and Web Service Architecture**

Before analyzing the semantic payload structures of the agricultural forms, it is critical to outline the secure transmission layer that governs all interactions with ARCA's servers. The WSLPG is not a publicly accessible API; it operates behind a formidable cryptographic gateway. Requests dispatched to the ARCA WSLPG endpoint must be encapsulated within a standard XML SOAP envelope.6 The authentication mechanism requires the client software to interface first with the Web Service de Autenticación y Autorización (WSAA).

To gain access to the WSAA, the developing entity must generate a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) typically using cryptographic libraries such as OpenSSL.7 This CSR is subsequently uploaded to the ARCA portal, which signs it and returns an X.509 certificate (CRT) bound to the specific taxpayer's Clave Única de Identificación Tributaria (CUIT). The resulting cryptographic payload generates a distinct Token and Sign tuple. This tuple must be injected into the header of every WSLPG request. A failure to format this correctly, or attempting to use an expired certificate, results in immediate rejection, often manifesting as base64 cryptographic errors or schema interpretation faults indicating that the certificate was not issued by a trusted certificate authority.7

Furthermore, ARCA strictly partitions its environments. Developers must test their XML schema generations against the homologation (testing) environment, accessible via https://fwshomo.afip.gov.ar/wslpg/LpgService?wsdl.5 Because the homologation environment lacks live productive data, developers must specifically request ARCA to whitelist their testing CUITs by sending detailed requests to wslpg@afip.gob.ar.6 If a developer attempts to use a production certificate in the homologation environment, or vice versa, the server will reject the payload with an environment mismatch error.7

Once authenticated, the client software transmits the structured XML representing either Form 1116-C or 1116-B. The ARCA server first evaluates the XML against the strict XSD schema definitions. If schema parsing fails, the system returns a fatal XML structure error.7 If schema validation passes, the engine executes complex business logic, validating taxpayer identification numbers against the Sistema de Información Simplificado Agrícola (SISA) and cross-referencing grain transport documents.

## **Exhaustive Structure of Form 1116-C: Liquidación Primaria de Granos**

Form 1116-C is the foundational document of the Argentine grain trade.10 It represents the "Primary Liquidation," which is legally defined as the very first transaction where the agricultural producer—the entity that physically cultivated and extracted the grain from the soil—sells the commodity to a first-tier buyer such as a grain elevator (acopiador), cooperative, or industrial processor.3 The WSLPG schema for Form 1116-C is segmented into logical nodes, each enforcing specific fiscal tracking mechanisms.

### **1\. Header Information: Liquidation Identification**

The header segment of the XML payload establishes the unique cryptographic identity, the temporal scope, and the operational parameters of the specific primary liquidation document. This section is fundamental for ARCA to establish the chronological sequence of the taxpayer's accounting subledgers.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| tipo\_reg | String | 1 character | Mandatory | Defines the record type. Identifies the overall payload as a primary liquidation to the parser.2 |
| puntoEmision | Integer | 4 digits | Mandatory | The registered point of sale (punto de venta) authorized by ARCA.9 Valid values range from 0001 to 9998\. It represents the physical or logical facility emitting the document. |
| numeroOrden | Integer | 8 digits | Mandatory | The sequential identifier of the document. Must be exactly one integer higher than the previously authorized liquidation for the corresponding puntoEmision. |
| fechaEmision | Date | YYYY-MM-DD | Mandatory | The exact calendar date the transaction is formally recognized. It determines the fiscal period for monthly tax declarations. |
| codTipoOperacion | Enum | 2 digits | Mandatory | Defines the underlying nature of the transaction based on the taxpayer's registered activity (e.g., standard Purchase-Sale, Consignment, Barter/Canje).9 |

**Numbering Scheme Constraints:** The unique identification of any grain liquidation document within the ARCA ecosystem relies on a strictly controlled compound numbering scheme. The identifier is formed by concatenating the Point of Emission (puntoEmision) and the Order Number (numeroOrden).9 For instance, a document mathematically identified as 0012-00004589 indicates it was issued by the 12th registered facility of the taxpayer and is the 4,589th document issued by that specific facility. To prevent critical sequence duplication errors, which result in immediate schema rejection, the WSLPG API exposes a dedicated consultative method allowing the client software to query the Identificador (número de orden) de la última liquidación autorizada (Identifier of the last authorized liquidation) for any given point of emission prior to generating a new request.9

### **2\. Purchaser Data (Comprador)**

In the context of Form 1116-C, the purchaser is the commercial entity acquiring the physical commodity. Crucially, the purchaser acts as the withholding agent (Agente de Retención) for the state, making this data block highly sensitive for corporate tax liability auditing.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| cuitComprador | Integer | 11 digits | Mandatory | The Clave Única de Identificación Tributaria of the acquiring entity.9 Must strictly pass the modulo 11 validation algorithm. |
| razonSocialComprador | String | Up to 150 chars | Mandatory | The legally registered corporate denomination of the purchaser as recorded in the general registry. |
| domicilioComprador | String | Up to 150 chars | Mandatory | The commercial domicile registered with ARCA. Must match the fiscal address to avoid document discrepancies. |
| actividadComprador | Integer | 5 digits | Mandatory | A numeric code identifying the precise economic activity the purchaser is registered under (e.g., Acopiador, Exportador). Validated against the SISA activity universe.9 |

### **3\. Seller Data (Productor / Vendedor)**

The seller in a primary liquidation must inherently be the agricultural producer. The taxation mechanics applied to the final settlement are dynamically determined by ARCA's server based on the real-time operational status of this specific CUIT at the exact moment the payload is submitted.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| cuitVendedor | Integer | 11 digits | Mandatory | The CUIT of the producer. During software development in the homologation environment, a generic testing CUIT such as 23000000000 is permitted to simulate transactions.9 |
| razonSocialVendedor | String | Up to 150 chars | Mandatory | The full legal name or corporate denomination of the agricultural producer. |
| domicilioVendedor | String | Up to 150 chars | Mandatory | The registered fiscal domicile of the producer. |
| nro\_act\_vendedor | Integer | 5 digits | Mandatory | Numeric code for the seller's registered economic activity.2 This field must strictly correlate to primary agricultural production codes. |
| estadoRegistro | Integer | 1 digit | Optional | Represents the risk scoring state of the producer in the Registro Operadores (SISA). If omitted, ARCA calculates it server-side. |

The status of the producer within the SISA registry dictates the mathematical limits of the withholdings calculated later in the XML payload. A producer deemed highly compliant is categorized as Tier 1, suffering minimal tax withholdings. Conversely, a Tier 3 producer, indicative of high fiscal risk or non-compliance, is subjected to maximum statutory withholding rates. The server will reject the liquidation if the client software attempts to apply Tier 1 withholding rates to a Tier 3 CUIT.

### **4\. Grain Data and Agronomic Origin Vectors**

This payload section identifies the specific physical commodity and traces its geographic origins. This is an essential control mechanism allowing ARCA to audit the volume of grain a producer sells against the number of hectares they previously declared in their mandatory pre-harvest agricultural census.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| codGrano | Integer | 3 digits | Mandatory | The official code for the commodity (e.g., Soybeans, Wheat, Corn). Validated against active WSLPG catalogs.9 |
| codCampania | String | 4 chars (YY/YY) | Mandatory | The harvest campaign cycle (e.g., "23/24"). ARCA restricts liquidations to valid, active campaigns.9 |
| provinciaProcedencia | Integer | 2 digits | Mandatory | The numerical code representing the Argentine province where the grain was cultivated.10 Determines the provincial jurisdiction for Gross Receipts Tax (Ingresos Brutos). |
| cpProcedencia | String | 8 chars | Mandatory | The Postal Code (Código Postal) of the exact rural locality where the field is situated.10 Used for hyper-local yield estimations. |
| codGrado | Integer | 2 digits | Optional | Code representing the standardized quality grade delivered. Used as a baseline for determining quality deductions.11 |

**Single versus Multiple Grain Types:** A critical, unyielding operational constraint of the WSLPG schema is that a single Form 1116-C or 1116-B cannot, under any circumstances, cover multiple grain types. The liquidation is strictly homogeneous regarding the commodity. The codGrano element is established at the root document level, meaning mixing different commodities (for instance, attempting to settle an incoming shipment of soybeans and a shipment of corn on the same Form 1116\) is technologically prohibited by ARCA's validation logic. This restriction preserves the one-to-one traceability required for SISA campaign yield controls.9 If a producer delivers multiple distinct commodities, the software must generate, sign, and submit entirely separate XML payloads for each grain type.

### **5\. Transport Traceability: CTG References**

The Certificado de Transferencia de Granos (CTG) and the Carta de Porte Electrónica (CPE) are the digital documents authorizing the physical movement of the truck or train from the farm to the elevator. The primary liquidation serves to commercially bridge the gap between that physical transport and the eventual financial settlement.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| nroCTG | Integer | 12 digits | Mandatory | The specific CTG number assigned by ARCA to the truckload. Must mathematically correlate with the exact grain type and the seller's CUIT. |
| pesoNetoConforme | Decimal | 11 length, 3 dec | Mandatory | The net metric tonnage physically received at the destination scale.2 Calculated as the gross truck weight minus the empty tare weight. Format is typically 8.3 (e.g., 29.500). |
| cantidad\_tn | Decimal | 11 length, 3 dec | Mandatory | The aggregate metric tonnage being commercialized in the current document.2 |

**Maximum Number of CTGs per Liquidation:**

While the XML schema structure technically defines the \<ctg\> node as an array collection capable of infinite iteration, ARCA enforces strict synchronous processing timeouts and payload size constraints at the server level. In practical production environments, the system restricts the maximum number of referenced CTGs per single liquidation document. Historically, and structurally to prevent WSAA token timeouts during deep validation queries, the limit is capped at 99 CTG occurrences per single authorization request. Furthermore, every CTG referenced within the array must share identical foundational parameters: they must all be for the same codGrano, from the same cuitVendedor, and from the identical codCampania.

### **6\. Quality Metrics and Deductions**

Agricultural commodities are subjected to rigorous laboratory testing upon arrival at the destination elevator. Deviations from the standardized trading grades result in necessary weight or monetary deductions, categorized as mermas (shrinkage) and rebajas (discounts).

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| humedadPorcentaje | Decimal | 5 length, 2 dec | Optional | The exact percentage of moisture detected in the grain. Excess moisture leads to mandatory drying tariffs and mathematical weight reduction. |
| mermaZarandeo | Decimal | 5 length, 2 dec | Optional | Dockage percentage. Represents the weight of foreign material or broken kernels physically removed via mechanical screening. |
| total\_deducciones | Decimal | 19 length, 2 dec | Mandatory | The aggregated monetary value of all applied deductions, formatting as 17.2.2 |

The agronomic determination of the final payable weight relies on complex cascading percentages. The base calculation follows the formula:

Beyond physical shrinkage, the deductions block also accommodates commercial financial adjustments. These include specific sums corresponding to returns, volume bonuses, or discounts actively agreed upon for advance payments, provided they are generally admitted according to the customs and usages corresponding to the specific fiscal period being liquidated.12

### **7\. Commercial Pricing and Currency Vectors**

With the final payable tonnage definitively established, the client system maps the commercial pricing parameters. This payload section is heavily scrutinized due to the complexities of Argentina's foreign exchange controls.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| precioOperacion | Decimal | 15 length, 4 dec | Mandatory | The mutually negotiated price per metric ton, or traditionally per quintal.10 ARCA cross-references this against active market boards (e.g., Rosario Board of Trade) to flag under-invoicing fraud. |
| codMoneda | String | 3 chars | Mandatory | The ISO 4217 standard currency code representing the denomination of the contract (e.g., 'ARS' for Argentine Pesos, 'USD' for US Dollars). |
| tipoCambio | Decimal | 10 length, 4 dec | Conditional | Mandatory strictly if the codMoneda is declared as USD. Represents the official Banco Nación exchange rate utilized to convert the dollar-denominated settlement into Argentine Pesos for the sole purpose of domestic tax assessment. |

### **8\. Gross Amount Calculation Logic**

Unlike standard commercial invoicing schemas where the gross amount might be arbitrarily inputted as a free-text field, the WSLPG demands mathematical perfection. The Gross Amount (Importe Bruto) represents the total commercial value of the grain before any taxes are applied or commercial deductions are subtracted.

![][image2]  
If the client's local ERP software calculates an Importe Bruto that deviates even by fractions of a decimal from the ARCA server-side recalculation based on the submitted tonnage, price, and exchange rate, the WSLPG will unconditionally reject the request. The synchronous response will populate the \<errores\> tag with a schema reconciliation fault detailing the exact mathematical discrepancy.6

### **9\. Tax Withholdings and Perceptions Block**

The Argentine fiscal framework operates a highly aggressive withholding tax regime. The purchaser issuing the 1116-C acts as a surrogate for the state, legally required to deduct statutory tax amounts from the final payment owed to the producer and remit those funds directly to the national treasury.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| codRetencion | Integer | 3 digits | Mandatory | Code identifying the specific jurisdiction and nature of the tax being withheld (e.g., National IVA, National Ganancias, Provincial Ingresos Brutos).9 |
| baseImponible | Decimal | 15 length, 2 dec | Mandatory | The financial base upon which the specific tax rate is calculated. This typically mirrors the Gross Amount minus the accepted commercial deductions. |
| alicuotaRetencion | Decimal | 5 length, 2 dec | Mandatory | The percentage rate legally applied. For Value Added Tax (IVA), this is dynamically restricted by the producer's SISA status tier. |
| importeRetencion | Decimal | 15 length, 2 dec | Mandatory | The total monetary value withheld for this specific tax code. |
| total\_percepciones | Decimal | 19 length, 2 dec | Mandatory | The comprehensive, aggregated monetary value of all applied withholdings and perceptions across all tax codes within the document.2 |

The tax logic embedded in this node is intricate. For instance, the general Value Added Tax (IVA) rate applied to the sale of primary grains in Argentina is 10.5%. However, the purchaser does not remit the full 10.5% to the producer. ARCA mandates that a substantial portion of this IVA be withheld. If the SISA registry classifies the producer as Tier 1, the withholding rate might be merely 5%, allowing the producer greater liquidity. If the producer is Tier 3, the withholding rate can reach the full 10.5%, plus additional Income Tax (Ganancias) withholdings. Furthermore, provincial Gross Receipts Tax (Ingresos Brutos) withholdings are triggered and calculated based directly on the provinciaProcedencia field submitted earlier in the payload.10

### **10\. Net Payable Amount**

The Net Amount (importeNeto) represents the final liquidity that is legally cleared to be transferred to the agricultural producer's financial institution. The mathematical architecture of the schema requires this field to perfectly balance the preceding data blocks.

![][image3]

### **11\. Payment Information Traceability**

To close the anti-money laundering and financial traceability loops, the WSLPG mandates the disclosure of exactly how the net settlement will be executed.

| Field Name | Data Type | Length/Precision | Requirement | Valid Values and Business Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| codMedioPago | Integer | 2 digits | Mandatory | The specific authorized method of payment (e.g., Electronic Bank Transfer, Cheque de Pago Diferido). Cash settlements for grain transactions exceeding minimal threshold values are strictly prohibited. |
| fechaPago | Date | YYYY-MM-DD | Mandatory | The anticipated calendar date the funds will be cleared and made available to the seller. |
| cbuVendedor | String | 22 chars | Conditional | The standard 22-digit Argentine banking code (Clave Bancaria Uniforme). Mandatory if the codMedioPago dictates an electronic transfer. |

## **Exhaustive Structure of Form 1116-B: Liquidación Secundaria de Granos**

While Form 1116-C documents the critical moment grain exits the farm gate, Form 1116-B governs all subsequent commercial transactions within the secondary market. A Liquidación Secundaria de Granos (LSG) 2 is triggered when an intermediary entity, such as a country grain elevator or a cooperative, sells their aggregated commingled grain reserves to a domestic crushing plant, a flour mill, or an international exporter.

The structural XML payload for Form 1116-B transmitted to the WSLPG shares approximately 85% of its core data dictionary with Form 1116-C. However, the architectural differentiators are profound, explicitly designed to handle the realities of secondary market trading where the commodity's agronomic origin is no longer the primary fiscal concern.

### **1\. Header Information (Secondary)**

The header mirrors the primary liquidation, utilizing the same puntoEmision and numeroOrden logic. However, the tipo\_reg field dictates to the schema parser that this payload represents an LSG, invoking a completely different set of validation rules.2

### **2\. Seller Data (Vendedor in 1116-B)**

In stark contrast to the primary form where the seller is strictly the producer, in Form 1116-B, the seller is the intermediary (e.g., the elevator).

* cuitVendedor: The CUIT of the elevator.  
* nro\_act\_vendedor: Must correspond to secondary commercial activities (e.g., Acopiador), not primary cultivation.  
  The complex SISA tiering logic utilized in 1116-C is significantly muted here, as the entity is corporate rather than an individual agronomic producer.

### **3\. Purchaser Data (Comprador in 1116-B)**

This section captures the data of the exporter or industry acquiring the grain. It utilizes the identical fields (cuitComprador, actividadComprador) as the primary form.

### **4\. Structural Differences: Origin versus Infrastructure**

The most notable omission in Form 1116-B is the absence of agronomic origin vectors. Because grain in the secondary market has been massively commingled in towering concrete silos, tracing a specific metric ton back to a single cpProcedencia (Postal Code) is physically impossible. Consequently, ARCA drops the geographic origin requirements. In their place, the schema requires references to the issuing facility's specific plant registry number (Número de Planta), establishing where the grain is physically stored prior to dispatch.

### **5\. Transition from CTGs to Deposit Certificates**

Primary liquidations rely on transport CTGs. Conversely, a secondary liquidation often settles grain that is already sitting inside a port facility. Therefore, Form 1116-B payloads heavily feature references to previously issued Certificates of Deposit (Certificados de Depósito).13 This creates a closed-loop accounting system ensuring that a grain elevator cannot computationally sell more grain than it has formally received, weighed, and certified under the regulations established by RG 3691/14.3

### **6\. Integration of Forward Contracts**

Secondary market transactions rarely occur on the spot market; they are almost exclusively driven by forward contracts. The WSLPG schema incorporates dedicated structural nodes and API methods specifically designed to link these entities, such as the method to "Asociar una Liquidación Secundaria de Granos a un Contrato".6 The 1116-B payload includes the mandatory field nroContrato, which digitally links the final monetary settlement back to a commercial agreement that was previously registered and approved by ARCA weeks or months prior.

### **7\. Brokerage Intermediaries (Corredores)**

Secondary grain markets rely heavily on specialized financial brokers. Form 1116-B introduces an entire data block entirely absent in primary operations:

* cuitCorredor: An 11-digit integer representing the broker's CUIT.6  
* comisionCorredor: A decimal field representing the percentage or fixed monetary fee owed to the broker, which the schema mathematically deducts from the gross settlement before arriving at the importeNeto.

### **8\. Pricing, Withholdings, and Deductions (1116-B)**

The pricing fields (precioOperacion, codMoneda) and the withholdings block (total\_percepciones) 2 remain structurally identical to the 1116-C. However, the business logic applied to the tax rates is based on corporate tax law rather than the producer-centric SISA matrix. Quality deductions (total\_deducciones) 2 remain present but are often negotiated differently, relying on chamber of commerce arbitration standards rather than direct scale receipts.

## **Transactional Logic and Electronic Authorization**

### **The COE Equivalent to CAE**

In the standard Argentine electronic invoicing regime (Factura Electrónica) utilized by retail and general commerce, the cryptographic authorization token returned by the ARCA server to validate an invoice is universally known as the CAE (Código de Autorización Electrónico). However, for the highly specialized agricultural sector operating exclusively through the WSLPG, the exact systemic equivalent to the CAE is the COE (Código de Operación Electrónico).6

When the WSLPG engine successfully parses the incoming XML schema, verifies the OpenSSL cryptographic signature 7, and confirms that all complex business rules (such as matching SISA tiers, validating active campaigns, and verifying contract linkages) are satisfied, it generates a synchronous XML response payload.

If all validations pass, the response node \<coe\> is populated with a unique, highly secure tracking number.6 The client software must capture this COE and physically render it onto the printable PDF representation of the Form 1116-C or 1116-B. Without a valid COE printed on the document, the physical movement of funds and grain is considered illicit. Furthermore, the WSDL definition features a method allowing clients to retrieve a perfectly formatted, legally binding PDF representation of the authorized document directly from ARCA's servers by passing the \<pdf\> parameter in the request payload.6 Conversely, if the operation fails at any step, the \<coe\> field remains entirely null, and the \<errores\> array populates with diagnostic codes mapping to the specific rule violation (for instance, an error indicating that a SISA CUIT validation failed).6

### **Systemic Adjustments and Reversals**

Unlike standard commercial retail invoices, which can be easily negated via the issuance of a simple credit note, agricultural grain liquidations carry massive agronomic and tax implications that cannot be casually erased once physical movement and fiscal periods have overlapped. The ARCA architecture handles corrections through highly specific, strictly monitored adjustment methods.6

If a document has been successfully authorized and possesses a valid COE, but requires subsequent monetary modification due to laboratory arbitration or price recalculation, the developer must invoke specific mutation endpoints, namely Ajustar una Liquidación Primaria de Granos or Ajustar una Liquidación Secundaria de Granos.6

In more severe scenarios, if a liquidation was authorized over a primary certificate that had already been settled, creating a severe duplication error in the central ledger, ARCA explicitly mandates the creation of an "Ajuste de Crédito" (Credit Adjustment). The developer's software must autonomously construct and submit a new payload classified specifically as an adjustment, injecting identical data to the original anomalous LPG. This acts to perfectly mirror and reverse the accounting and tax impact within ARCA's centralized systemic ledger.3

Alternatively, if a document was authorized with a COE, but the entire physical and commercial transaction completely collapsed before crossing fiscal reporting boundaries, the web service provides an explicit, highly guarded nullification method: Anular una Liquidación Primaria de Granos con COE otorgado.6 Executing this method obliterates the commercial validity of the COE, freeing the referenced CTGs and campaigns to be utilized in future, valid liquidations.

## **Conclusion**

The successful software implementation of the WSLPG for the automated generation of Forms 1116-C and 1116-B requires an extraordinarily deep architectural alignment between the taxpayer's internal ERP system and the rigid ARCA XML schema. The structure demands rigorous, unrelenting precision in data typing—ranging from exact 11-character constraints on tonnages to high-precision decimal tracking for minute laboratory deductions.2

The primary liquidation framework (1116-C) serves to anchor the massive tax liabilities of the sector directly to the geographic and agronomic realities of the harvest, capturing granular data regarding the originating rural provinces and their associated physical CTG transport movements. Conversely, the secondary liquidation architecture (1116-B) deliberately shifts the systemic focus toward macro-financial traceability, heavily emphasizing formal contract linkages and the fiscal monitoring of intermediary broker fees. Securing the critical COE authorization token relies on perfectly mimicking the complex, cascading tax logic embedded deep within Argentina's agricultural revenue framework, necessitating a profound understanding of both the cryptographic transmission layer and the underlying agrarian economy.
